We will show that the only function satisfying the conditions is the zero function.

Define

\[
g(z)=z^2 f(z), \qquad z\neq 0.
\]

Then \(g\) is analytic on \(\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\), and the given bound gives

\[
|g(z)|=|z|^2|f(z)|\le 5|z|^{2-\sqrt2}.
\]

Since \(2-\sqrt2>0\), we have

\[
\lim_{z\to 0} g(z)=0.
\]

Thus \(g\) has a removable singularity at \(0\), and extends to an entire function \(G\) with

\[
G(0)=0.
\]

Because \(G(0)=0\), the function

\[
h(z)=\frac{G(z)}{z}
\]

is also entire. For \(z\neq 0\),

\[
h(z)=\frac{z^2 f(z)}{z}=z f(z).
\]

Now estimate \(h\):

\[
|h(z)|=|z f(z)|\le 5|z|^{1-\sqrt2}.
\]

Since \(1-\sqrt2<0\), the right-hand side tends to \(0\) as \(|z|\to\infty\). In particular, \(h\) is bounded on \(\mathbb C\): for \(|z|\ge 1\),

\[
|h(z)|\le 5,
\]

and on compact sets an entire function is bounded. By Liouville’s theorem, \(h\) is constant. But \(h(z)\to 0\) as \(|z|\to\infty\), so that constant must be \(0\). Hence

\[
h\equiv 0.
\]

Therefore, for every \(z\neq 0\),

\[
z f(z)=0,
\]

so \(f(z)=0\). Thus the only admissible function is \(f\equiv 0\), and consequently

\[
|f(1)|=0.
\]

The supremum is therefore

\[
\boxed{0}
\]
